描述_ZN: Page from "Poem for the Longevity of Zun Weng", Ming dynasty, inscribed by Qian Pu on blue paper, album, 28.1 cm in length and 40.1 cm in width, in regular script, 14 lines.　　Commentary: The earth is adjacent to the East China Sea and connected to Penglai. The green birds come from beyond the clouds, and the man in ribbon clothes comes from the edge of the sun. The light is divided into rosy brocade poems, and the color is filled with wine. Asking what is the age of longevity, the sixty-year old man is the first time to return.　　The scholar Ye Jun and the middle, the party thought of your father's first 60 years, wanting a goblet but not yet. I suddenly had a trip to Hunan, so I took a convenient way to satisfy my private needs. I wrote a poem for his birthday. This poem is written by Qian Pu, a member of the Hanlin family, at the beginning of the spring of the year of Zhengtong.　　Inscriptions of "Yunma Qian's original Pu" and "Baiyutang Seal" under the signature, and "Huating" seal at the head. The collection seal is inscribed with "Seal of the Sacred Collection of Gold, Stone, Calligraphy and Painting".　　This poem was written by Qian Pu for the 60th birthday of his father, "Ye Jun and Zhong". "Ye and Zhong" is Ye Sheng. The year "Zhengtong bing yin" is the eleventh year of the Ming dynasty (1446).　　The calligraphy of "Longevity Poem for Zun Weng" is strong and elegant, with a delicate and clear beauty. Qian Pu's calligraphy is based on Song Ke, and the lines of his strokes contain the meaning of chapter and grass strokes, with tough strokes, exposed peaks, and sharp strokes. The author's influence of the formal and rigid "pagoda style" calligraphy of the early Ming court can be seen from its out-of-regulation characteristics.
